title: What to Watch This Week: The Streaming Guide for May 25-31
excerpt: Dhanush directs himself on Netflix, Nicolas Cage goes noir on Prime Video, and Jolly LLB 3 finally hits OTT. Eight picks for the week.
body:
The last week of May is loaded. Between Tamil action landing on Netflix, a noir superhero experiment on Prime Video, and a courtroom comedy finally hitting OTT, there is enough to fill every evening through the weekend. Here is what is actually worth your time.

## Kara — Netflix (May 28)

Dhanush directed and stars in this rural Tamil action drama about a former village enforcer returning home to find his younger brother caught in a cycle of caste violence and land feuds. It made ₹50 crore theatrically on a ₹100 crore budget, which means Netflix is where most people will actually watch it. Available in five languages. If you have been waiting for Dhanush behind the camera again, this is it.

## Spider-Noir — Prime Video (May 27)

Nicolas Cage plays a retired superhero-turned-private-investigator in 1930s New York. It is moody, strange, and available in both black-and-white and colour. The reviews are strong — Cage is doing that thing where he fully commits to something weird and elevates it. Not Indian content, but it is the kind of show that will dominate group chats this week.

## Jolly LLB 3 — JioHotstar (May 29)

Akshay Kumar and Arshad Warsi face off as rival lawyers in Subhash Kapoor's courtroom comedy. Saurabh Shukla returns as Judge Tripathi. The theatrical run made ₹171 crore globally. If you missed it in theatres, this is the weekend watch — funny, populist, and built for family viewing.

## Brothers and Sisters — JioHotstar (May 27)

A Tamil family drama about four siblings raised by a conservative textile businessman. Generational conflict, financial disagreements, and the kind of sibling dynamics that hit close to home if you grew up in a joint family. New season, first-time watch — either way, it is comfort television with teeth.

## A Good Girl's Guide to Murder Season 2 — Netflix (May 27)

Emma Myers returns as Pip Fitz-Amobi, who launches a true-crime podcast that drags her into another dangerous investigation. The first season was a sleeper hit. This one goes darker — financial crimes, missing persons, and the personal toll of being the person who keeps digging.

## Cousins and Kalyanams — JioHotstar (May 29)

A Malayalam family drama that spans 26 years and seven weddings. Six cousins, broken engagements, inheritance fights, hidden affairs. If you grew up attending massive Indian weddings where every uncle had an opinion and every cousin had a secret, this is essentially a documentary.

## Dead Man's Wire — Netflix (May 28)

Gus Van Sant directs Bill Skarsgård as a financially ruined real estate developer who kidnaps a mortgage broker with a rigged shotgun. Based on a true story. Tense, claustrophobic, and the kind of thriller that makes you forget to breathe for 90 minutes.

## Satrangi: Badle Ka Khel — ZEE5 (Already streaming)

A Hindi crime drama set in rural Uttar Pradesh about a Launda Naach performer's son seeking revenge against a powerful upper-caste family. Anshumaan Pushkar and Kumud Mishra are both excellent. The reviews say it stretches in places, but the performances and the social commentary make it worth the watch. A genuine hidden gem if you like your crime stories rooted in real India.
